question: I'm a transfer student with 60 credits from community college. which gen ed requirements does Ramapo still make me take?
answer:
If at least 48 of your credits are from an accredited institution, Ramapo’s transfer-student rule requires Critical Reading and Writing 102, Quantitative Reasoning, Scientific Reasoning, and one course in each of two distribution categories: Culture and Creativity, Values and Ethics, and Social Systems and Society. First Year Seminar, Global Awareness, Historical Perspectives, Social Science Inquiry, and Studies in the Arts and Humanities are waived under this rule. [4][5]

Your exact remaining courses depend on the transfer evaluation and advisement; during academic advisement, you’ll be advised of applicable waivers and remaining requirements. [5] For a particular course’s potential equivalency, contact the Vice Provost; if approved, the approval goes to Admissions to update the appropriate systems. [10]

If you completed an A.A. or A.S. at a New Jersey community college, Admissions says you are waived from General Education requirements after submitting a final official transcript showing the conferred degree. [12] Another page says an A.A. or A.S. from a New Jersey community college fulfills Gen Ed for a four-year Ramapo degree. [13] An A.A.S. does not qualify for a full waiver; courses are evaluated individually. [12]

Office of the Provost: provost@ramapo.edu; (201) 684-7330. [10] Admissions: admissions@ramapo.edu; (201) 684-7300. [12]

question: Im a biology major and want to add a second major in psychology. what courses would the psych major require?
answer:
The Psychology major is a Bachelor of Arts. [2]
Required: PSYC 101 Introduction to Psychology; PSYC 242 Statistics; PSYC 303 Research Methods in Psychology and PSYC 304 Data Analysis in Psychology. [2]
Choose one course in each category: [2]
• Social/Organizational: PSYC 226 Social Psychology or PSYC 345 Workplace Psychology.
• Cognition/Perception: PSYC 202 Psychology of Learning, PSYC 209 Psychology of Perception, or PSYC 227 Cognitive Psychology.
• Developmental: PSYC 212 Psychology of Aging, PSYC 241 Developmental Psychology, PSYC 263 Child Psychology, or PSYC 347 Adolescent Psychology.
• Socio-cultural: PSYC 231 Multicultural Psychology, PSYC 239 Cross-Cultural Psychology, PSYC 307 Psychology of Yoga, PSYC 311 Psychology of Gender, PSYC 335 Sexualities and Gender Identities: LGBTQA+, or PSYC 349 Psychology of Women.
• Clinical: PSYC 314 Psychopathology, PSYC 321 Theories of Personality, or PSYC 357 Childhood Disorders.
• Brain/Behavior: PSYC 310 Neuropsychology, PSYC 352 Behavioral Neuroscience, PSYC 353 Cognitive Neuroscience, or PSYC 355 Neuropsychopharmacology.
• Fieldwork/Independent Research: PSYC 319 Adult Psychology Fieldwork, PSYC 320 Psychopathology Fieldwork, PSYC 339 Fieldwork with Adolescents, PSYC 358 Childhood Disorders Fieldwork, PSYC 367 Fieldwork with Children, PSYC 368 Fieldwork in Forensic Psychology, or PSYC 472 Advanced Research.
• Capstone: PSYC 430 Capstone Seminar Topics in Psychology; PSYC 431 Child Maltreatment; PSYC 432 Psychology of Cults; PSYC 433 Psychopathy; PSYC 434 Cultural Nature of Development; PSYC 436 Psychoanalytic Thought—Understanding the Unconscious; PSYC 437 Psychology of Happiness; PSYC 438 Social Justice and Psychology; PSYC 439 Phenomenological Psychology; PSYC 440 Eyewitness Memory; PSYC 450 Cognitive Development; or PSYC 451 Black Psychology. [2]
Also listed: “Additional Psychology Course - Select 1 Course,” with no choices specified. Career Pathways lists PATH 001 twice and PATH 003 once. [2]
For two majors, no more than half the courses may double-count, and all writing-intensive courses required for Psychology must be completed. [6]

question: whats the difference between a minor and a certificate here
answer:
A minor is an undergraduate supplement to your major, intended to add depth and breadth. It must include 16–24 credits, counting non-General Education prerequisites and excluding lab science course credits. Courses for your primary or secondary major may overlap, but no more than half the minor’s credits may count toward the major. [4][6]

“Academic Certificates are organized, coherent programs of study usually comprised of credit-bearing courses.” They may also include non-credit learning experiences. Levels include undergraduate certificates, graduate certificates requiring at least 9 credits beyond the Bachelor’s level, and doctoral certificates requiring at least 12 credits beyond the Master’s level. They are not graduation requirements and are removed from the degree audit. [3]

Ramapo also distinguishes Professional Certificates: these consist entirely of not-for-credit learning experiences, are not differentiated by level, and are not noted on transcripts; the Registrar does not administer or issue them. [5]

For questions about how a particular certificate is recorded, contact the Office of the Provost at provost@ramapo.edu or (201) 684-7330. [3][5]

Sources: [3](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#certificate-programs1) [4](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#integrity-of-degree-programs1) [5](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#certificate-programs1) [6](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#integrity-of-degree-programs1)

question: how many credits is econ 101 and what does it cover
answer:
ECON 101 MICROECONOMICS is 4 credits. [1] It studies the motivations, incentives and constraints on individuals in market decision-making, and how their decisions affect society. It covers how consumer and producer decisions determine prices and allocate goods and services; the supply-and-demand paradigm; utility theory; market structure; and government intervention. The course develops an analytical perspective for thinking critically about market systems and social objectives, and includes economic terms and models, economists’ approaches to problems, issues of economic importance, and the effects of government policies on individuals. [1]
Prerequisite: CRWT 102 CRITICAL READING AND WRITING II or CRWT 102S CRITICAL READING AND WRITING II; may be taken concurrently with ECON 101. Attribute: ASB Writing Core (BWAC). [1]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/ECON101)

question: what is the Intellectual Inquiry or whatever its called gen ed thing, and how many courses is it
answer:
Ramapo’s General Education program is ten courses: four keystone courses, one course in each of four keystone categories, and one course in two of three distribution categories [3]. The keystone courses are First Year Seminar, Social Science Inquiry, Critical Reading & Writing 102, and Studies in the Arts & Humanities; CRWT 102 must be taken within the first 64 credits [3]. The keystone categories are Global Awareness, Historical Perspectives, Scientific Reasoning, and Quantitative Reasoning; Quantitative Reasoning must be taken within the first 64 credits [3]. question: I'm adding a second major in political science, what's the recommended sequence of courses for it, and what's the min number of credits to finish both majors
answer:
The Political Science BA recommended plan is for students admitted to the major during the 2026–2027 academic year. It lists only the first year:
• First Year, Fall Semester (total 16 credits): INTD 101 - FIRST YEAR SEMINAR (4); CRWT 102 - CRITICAL READING AND WRITING II (4); General Education Requirement (4); POLI 223 - AMERICAN GOVERNMENT+ (double counts as Distribution Category: - SOCIAL SYSTEMS AND SOCIETY) (4); PATH 001 - CAREER PATHWAYS MOD 1.
• First Year, Spring Semester (total 16 credits): - QUANTITATIVE REASONING (4); General Education Requirement (4); General Education Requirement (4); POLI 205 - COMPARATIVE POLITICS (4).
The plan states “Total Credits Required: 128 credits.” [1]

The pages don’t state the combined minimum credits to complete two majors. They say major requirements must total at least 40 credits [5], and for two majors, no more than half the courses may count toward both [2]. The 128-credit figure is the Political Science plan’s total, not a stated combined-minimum for two majors. [1]

The Office of the Provost is the likely contact for clarification: provost@ramapo.edu; (201) 684-7330. [2]
